verses.english: “Mendicants, this body doesn’t belong to you or to anyone else.

verses.pali: Purāṇamidaṁ, bhikkhave, kammaṁ abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ vedaniyaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
verses.english: It’s old deeds, and should be seen as produced by choices and intentions, as something to be felt.

verses.pali: Tatra kho, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti:
verses.english: A learned noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

verses.pali: ‘iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
verses.english: ‘When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

verses.pali: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati, yadidaṁ—
verses.english: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”
